request.system:
You verify one claim against evidence passages scraped from the cited sources. Judge only from the passages, never from your own knowledge.
Verdicts:
- supported: a passage states the claim's value, so a reader could confirm it from the quote alone. Equivalent wording counts ("$10 per user/month" supports "$10 per user per month").
- partial: a passage supports part of the claim, or gives a materially different qualification (a different number, a range, an older date, a different plan or product).
- unsupported: the passages are on topic but do not state the value, or they contradict it.
- no_evidence: the passages are irrelevant or empty.
A passage that only mentions a word in another sense (e.g. a product name in a feature list) does not support a claim about it.
evidence_quote MUST be copied character-for-character from one passage: the shortest span that shows the value (under 300 characters). Use null for unsupported/no_evidence unless a passage contradicts the claim, in which case quote the contradiction.
reason: one sentence. If the passage contradicts the claim, say what it actually says.
request.user:
Research question: What major changes did Tailwind CSS v4.0 introduce?
Claim: Tailwind CSS v4.0 introduced a @starting‑style variant for transition‑on‑enter without JavaScript.
Value being checked: "@starting‑style variant for transition‑on‑enter without JavaScript"

<passage source="https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4">
…

[Tailwind CSS v4.0]

<!-- -->

- Container queries — first-class APIs for styling elements based on their container size, no plugins required.
- New 3D transform utilities — transform elements in 3D space directly in your HTML.
- Expanded gradient APIs — radial and conic gradients, interpolation modes, and more.
- @starting-style support — a new variant you can use to create enter and exit transitions, without the need for JavaScript.
- not-\* variant — style an element only when it doesn't match another variant, custom selector, or media or feature query.
- Even more new utilities and variants — including support for `color-scheme`, `field-sizing`, complex shadows, `inert`, and more.

…

[Tailwind CSS v4.0 > @starting-style support]

The new `starting` variant adds support for the new CSS `@starting-style` feature, making it possible to transition element properties when an element is first displayed:

…

With `@starting-style`, you can finally animate elements as they appear on the page without the need for any JavaScript at all. Browser support probably isn't quite there yet for most teams, but we're getting close!
</passage>

response: {"verdict":"supported","best_source_url":"https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4","evidence_quote":"@starting-style support — a new variant you can use to create enter and exit transitions, without the need for JavaScript.","reason":"The passage states Tailwind CSS v4.0 added @starting-style support as a new variant for enter and exit transitions without JavaScript, matching the claim."}
